To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIV + adults on cART therapy have lower performance than healthy adults in the domains of learning and attention/working memory.
HIV + adults, on cART therapy, have a significantly lower cognitive performance in the domains of working memory and learning, as compared to healthy controls.
HIV + adults on cART therapy have a poorer performance in attention/working memory and learning than a healthy comparison group, and this is more pronounced in older HIV + participants.

the HIV +group in this study had a lower cognitive performance in the domains of learning, and attention/working memory than the healthy control group.
, despite cART therapy, a certain cognitive deficit remains a problem for HIV + adults, which should not be neglected in the clinical practice.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV infection in the era of cART is associated with a lower performance in the domains of working memory, attention, and verbal learning.

HIV + adults on cART therapy are at a risk of developing cognitive deficits, which may be a consequence of the HIV infection itself, as well as the synergistic interaction between aging and HIV infection.
HIV + people on cART therapy are not cognitively intact, and that they are more prone to age-associated neurocognitive decline than healthy subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV + persons, even those with good clinical control of the illness and with a good subjective experience of cognitive function, should be routinely screened for cognitive impairment.

the cognitive profile of HIV + subjects on cART therapy in Serbia is similar to that of HIV + patients in developed countries, and that the cognitive profile in HIV + patients on cART is similar to that in HIV + subjects not on cART therapy.

a more thorough neuropsychological assessment of HIV + subjects should be performed in order to identify and treat the cognitive deficits in a timely manner, and thus prevent the negative consequences of the illness.
